The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aa71c4d9d146861fc09d63363e4c8fb8286719fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

The dispatching seat's own conclusions were not read as input. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Nothing was posted to GitHub.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.**

- RIGHT. `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.revertStoredPackage` (packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:23837) is a new public async method on a class the entry exports (packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts:3). The class is reached from the package's `exports["."]` types (packages/metadata-protocol/package.json). Adding it widens the published surface.
- RIGHT. `packageScopedRowWhere` (packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts:406) stays off the entry. index.ts re-exports only `SysMetadataRepository`, `resetEnvWritableMetadataTypes` and five types from that module (index.ts:153 to :160). There is no star re-export of it anywhere in index.ts. The docblock's claim at sys-metadata-repository.ts:403 holds. `discardDraftInItsScope` is `private` (protocol.ts:23769).
- RIGHT. The changeset sentence "The only change to the public surface is this one added method" (.changeset/22090-metadata-protocol-revert-stored-package.md:13) matches the diff.

**Membership.**

- RIGHT. `listDrafts` now builds its where through `packageScopedRowWhere(this.organizationId, 'draft', filter)` (sys-metadata-repository.ts:1285). The function sets, in order, `state`, then `$or` of the caller's organization and `organization_id: null` when the organization is non-null, else `organization_id: null`, then `type`, then `package_id` (sys-metadata-repository.ts:406 to :431). The base `listDrafts` built exactly those keys in exactly that order with the same values (merge-base `bafb58bb08`, sys-metadata-repository.ts:1241 to :1259). So `discardPackageDrafts` (protocol.ts:23717) reads the same drafts as before. Its per-draft delete is the same `deleteMetaItem` call with the same five arguments, now inside `discardDraftInItsScope` (protocol.ts:23769 to :23786). `discardPackageDrafts` answers as before.
- RIGHT. The active-row read `packageScopedRowWhere(orgId, 'active', { packageId })` (protocol.ts:23853) cannot see rows another organization owns. A non-null `orgId` yields `$or` of that organization and env-wide. A null `orgId` yields env-wide only. No arm matches a third organization. The door pin at packages/runtime/src/package-revert-stored-members.integration.test.ts:263 holds this at the door.
- NOTE, not wrong. The revert acts on the drafts the caller's organization sees, not on every draft of the package in storage. Another organization's draft of the same package stays. That is the rule `discardPackageDrafts` has always had, and the docblock states it (protocol.ts:23812 to :23815). The changeset's "every draft of the package" (metadata-protocol changeset:12) is bounded by its first bullet, "the same predicate `listDrafts` uses". Accurate as scoped.

**The door** (packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, revert branch :1893 to :1925).

- RIGHT. `requireManageMetadata` runs at :1894, before `resolveProtocol` (:1907) and before any read.
- RIGHT. The organization is `deps.resolveActiveOrganizationId(_context)` (:1910), the same source the discard-drafts door reads (:1809). Both spread it only when truthy.
- RIGHT. The revert passes `packageId` and `organizationId` only (:1911 to :1914). It reads no body `actor`. Discard-drafts does forward `body?.actor` (:1813). The revert door read no body at base, so its request contract is unchanged (.changeset/22090-runtime-revert-studio-package.md:12).
- RIGHT. `stored: false` falls through to `metadataService.revertPackage(id)` (:1920 to :1923), the base text unchanged. An unknown id answers the manager's own 404 (packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts:2092 to :2099 at base; test:279). A code-shipped package with no stored row answers the manager's own verdict (test:289 and :300). The `typeof` guard at :1908 keeps a protocol without the verb on the base path.
- ESCALATED, not blocking. A code-shipped package with an org overlay draft bound to it in `sys_metadata`. The dev measured 409 at base and at head with different sentences (6043377779 `out_of_scope_findings` second entry; PR body acceptance note 2). I confirm that reading for a code package the registry has never published: base answers the manager's 409 (metadata-manager.ts:2103 to :2110), head answers the protocol's 409 (protocol.ts:23864 to :23871). There is a variant the dev did not measure. The same package after `POST /packages/:id/publish` (packages.ts:1459 to :1466, which calls `MetadataManager.publishPackage`) has `publishedDefinition` on its registry members. At base, revert reached `revertPackage`, found them published, restored each member and answered 200 (metadata-manager.ts:2112 to :2121). At head, the protocol sees one stored draft and no active stored row, throws the 409 at protocol.ts:23864 to :23871 before the manager is asked, restores nothing, and the sentence "has never been published" is false for that package. So one reachable combination changes status, 200 to 409. The precondition is narrow: the manager collects only members carrying an authored `packageId` or `package` key (metadata-manager.ts:2067), so a stamp-only code package never reached the 200 arm at base either (the dev's finding (a) in 6043377779). The combination is a hybrid, registry members plus a stored overlay draft, which neither triage's four pins (6040669927) nor the card's reproduction covers, and its semantics is the question triage deferred to its foreseen follow-up ("whether a code baseline counts as published"). It does not block this PR. It must be named on that follow-up card with the reproduction above when the card is filed. The dispatching seat owns the filing.

**The 409.**

- RIGHT. `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is a member of the standard catalog (packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:95) and is the standard code for status 409 (errors.zod.ts:189). It is the same code and status `MetadataManager.revertPackage` throws (metadata-manager.ts:2107 to :2108 at base). No ledger row and no sweep entry is owed: packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts carries no row for the manager's identical producer, because a registered code drops out of the sweep (scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs header, "which makes the site disappear from the scan").
- RIGHT. The door catches with `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)` (packages.ts:1917). `HttpDispatcher.errorFromThrown` (packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts:1112) calls `resolveThrownHttpError` (packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, that function), which reads `.status` first and a registered `.code` second, and withholds nothing below 500. So the wire carries 409 and `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the sentence. Test:237 pins status, code and the sentence prefix at the door.

**Partial failure.**

- RIGHT. A refused draft propagates out of the loop (protocol.ts:23875 to :23878) after the drafts before it were deleted. The docblock states it in plain words: "Drafts discarded before the refusal stay discarded, as they do in discardPackageDrafts" (protocol.ts:23834 to :23835). The TSDoc ships in the entry declarations, so the method's consumer reads it there.
- NOTE. The metadata-protocol changeset states the failure mode, "A refused draft fails the call with that refusal's own code and status" (:12), but not that earlier drafts stay discarded. The PR body's acceptance note 3 does. One clause short. Not false.

**Unprovisioned store.** RIGHT. The catch at protocol.ts:23857 to :23860 returns `stored: false` only when `rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned` returns, and that helper returns only for `isMissingTableError`; every other failure is rethrown classified. The read-seam discriminator is the declared one.

**Accept set.** No request or response schema changes. The door's response stays `{ success: true }` (packages.ts:1915 and :1923). `PackagesDomainProtocol` gains an optional `revertStoredPackage` typed from the producer's own method (packages.ts:198, import at :56). That type is not exported from packages/runtime/src/index.ts, which exports nothing from `domains/packages`, so the runtime's published declarations do not move. The runtime's new import is `import type` and is erased at build.

**Tests.** The door pin covers triage's pins: (a) test:198, :213, :226; (b) test:237; (c) test:279; (d) test:289 and :300; and the two organization pins, test:251 and :263. packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-vetted-org-source.test.ts:339 adds the revert door to the roster of doors that read the vetted organization, with a double at :126. The new test imports only workspace packages the runtime manifest already declares (`@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`). No filesystem read escapes the package.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. RIGHT. One added public method on an exported class is "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface" and "takes at least `minor`" (.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:754 to :759; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, "`yes` takes at least `minor`"). The level axis reads it against the two levels and reaches `discharged`, one moved package at `minor` and one at `patch`, exit 0 (scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1515 to :1528). `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- The claim's and triage's `Clause-②: no` described a `metadata-manager.ts` fix that was never written. The diff is a different act. The dev measured the built declarations base against head (6043377779 `clause_2`); I confirm the same reading from the source entry. Option A of the open question is right. Option B would grade a widening `patch` and declare it `no`, which pr-automation.yml:754 to :759 forbids.
- Changesets, sentence by sentence. Metadata-protocol changeset: the title matches the signature at protocol.ts:23837 to :23844; bullet 1 matches the shared predicate (sys-metadata-repository.ts:406, :1285; protocol.ts:23853); bullet 2 matches protocol.ts:23857 to :23862, the unprovisioned arm included; bullet 3 matches :23864 to :23871, and "Nothing is touched" holds because the throw precedes the loop; bullet 4 matches :23873 to :23879 with the two notes in ① (scope of "every draft", the partial-state clause); bullet 5 matches ① Public surface and Membership. That covers a code-shipped package and an unknown id (404). It is also what happens when the protocol does not provide `revertStoredPackage`", matches packages.ts:1908 and :1920 to :1923 as scoped by "no stored row"; the hybrid in ① has a stored row and is outside that sentence; bullet 4 matches the unchanged request and the `{ success: true }` response.
